key_insight: Temporally correlated leakage limits quantum error correction, but a walking stability circuit suppresses it and lowers the logical error floor by two orders of magnitude.
engineering_relevance: Suppressing higher-state leakage and adapting syndrome-extraction duration could improve the reliability and time efficiency of fault-tolerant quantum processors.
method: Scale surface-code stability experiments from 3×3 to 7×7 patches on a 105-qubit Willow processor.
Model heating to |3⟩ and higher-state transport with a parameter-free, device-level leakage model.
Implement a walking stability circuit and evaluate decoder-confidence-based adaptive termination offline.
evidence_signal: Experiments achieved temporal block suppression μ_T = 1.47 ± 0.25 and a walking-circuit logical error floor ≤3.20×10⁻⁸ at 60 cycles; offline adaptive termination reduced spacetime logical error by 38% and time overhead by 34% versus the optimal fixed-cycle strategy.
watch_item: Ionizing-radiation bursts limit the remaining error floor, and adaptive termination was evaluated offline rather than demonstrated in real-time control.
paper_title: Resolving and Suppressing Temporally Correlated Noise in Quantum Error Correction
